messages:
incident-bot: Alert: SLO_egress_error_rate (eu-central-1) breached at 06:12 UTC. Auto-page sent to #incidents-oncall.
Amy Chen: paging in, looking at alerts. Seeing a spike in PrivateLink egress errors to customer ACME in eu-central-1.
Pete Alvarez: saw BGP flaps on our transit routers into AZ-b. Possible asymmetric path to customer SD-WAN.
Jordan Park: adding context — embeddings and auth requests from ACME are timing out then succeeding; 500ms->5s variability.
Leah Gomez: ACME NOC on standby, they report degraded connectivity from their SD-WAN edges to our PrivateLink endpoints since ~06:05 UTC.
ACME NOC: Confirmed, we see some routes prefer ISP-B via partner handoff and return traffic lands on ISP-A, packet loss ~8-12%.
Amy Chen: running quick traceroutes to one affected endpoint:
```
traceroute to pl-eu-1.redwood.private (10.4.22.77), 30 hops max
 1  10.10.0.1  0.2 ms
 2  198.51.100.6  2.1 ms (transit-router-eu-b)
 3  203.0.113.12  12.4 ms (isp-b)
 4  198.51.100.20  15.7 ms (edge-azb)
 5  10.4.22.77  16.0 ms
```
Pete Alvarez: looks like forward path uses ISP-B, return path logs indicate ISP-A. BFD flaps observed on peer id 64521->64522 around 06:03-06:09.
Jordan Park: past incidents runbook suggests checking ECMP/AWS peering route metrics + customer BGP weight. I'm spinning up tcpdump on az-b gateway to capture asymmetric packets.
Amy Chen: tcpdump snippet (filtered to src customer IP 198.51.200.0/24):
```
06:08:12.123456 IP 198.51.200.14 > 10.4.22.77: Flags [P.], seq 1:513, ack 1, win 229, length 512
06:08:12.123789 IP 10.4.22.77 > 198.51.200.14: Flags [.] ack 513, win 1024, length 0
06:08:12.124001 IP 198.51.200.14 > 10.4.22.77: Flags [P.], seq 513:1025, ack 1, length 512
```
Amy Chen: we see client->server on ISP-B, server->client via ISP-A. TCP retransmits and latency spikes.
Pete Alvarez: hypothesis: SD-WAN sends primary via ISP-B, but our egress traffic out of az-b prefers ISP-A due to recent weight adjust on transit. Could be a propagation delay on route withdraws.
Jordan Park: brief impact assessment: ~12% of ACME sessions see intermittent timeouts for auth calls (OIDC) and latency spikes on embeddings requests. Logged errors in the app gateway: 504/timeout surge.
Leah Gomez: ACME flagged customer-impact: their checkout flow fails for a subset of users. They're asking for a workaround they can apply on their side.
ACME NOC: Can we ask them to prefer a single IP-family/peer? We can pin traffic to ISP-A if that helps — but we need confirmation this won't loop.
Amy Chen: temp mitigation plan: 1) adjust our local egress route weights to prefer ISP-B for customer prefix 198.51.200.0/24 (so both directions use same transit) 2) ask ACME to prefer ISP-B or advertise higher local-pref to us 3) if needed, blackhole the flapping peer to force convergence.
Pete Alvarez: I can push a temporary BGP policy to increase MED on ISP-A for that prefix so ISP-B becomes preferred for egress from our side. Will do a dry-run then apply.
Jordan Park: rollback plan: remove policy after stab period (30m), monitor p99 latency and error rate. If issues persist, escalate to cloud provider peering team.
Amy Chen: executing step 1 now (applying policy on transit-azb).
deploy-bot: config-change: BGP policy update queued by pete.alvarez — ID bgp-policy-3371 — will apply in 30s window.
Pete Alvarez: applied bgp-policy-3371 to transit-router-eu-b. Waiting for propagation.
Amy Chen: monitoring metrics dashboard — egress error-rate dropping slowly. p50 latency improving. p99 still elevated.
ACME NOC: after your change we see more symmetric pathing, packet loss down to ~2-3%. Checkout errors reduced. Thanks.
Jordan Park: logging shows decreased 504s, embeddings latency stabilizing at ~220ms. Still watching for residual retransmits.
Amy Chen: posting quick note for next oncall: if error rate bounces back after propagation window (~06:45 UTC), revert policy and open ticket with ISP-A (they may have implemented accidental prepends).
Leah Gomez: customer comms: emailing ACME with summary and recommended temporary config (pin to ISP-B or add community set). I told them we'll follow up if we need to perform blackhole.
Pete Alvarez: creating a follow-up action item in tracker: NET-1429 — investigate root cause (BFD flaps on peer 64521/64522 + route propagation timing). Assign to Pete + Infra team.
Jordan Park: handing off to Jordan for next shift at 06:30 UTC. Summary: applied egress weight policy to favor ISP-B for ACME prefix; error rates decreased from ~12% impacted sessions to ~3%; keep monitoring for 30m, escalate to provider if oscillation returns.
Amy Chen: thanks, @Jordan. I've left the tcpdump capture and BGP logs in /var/log/incidents/4098765432/ for postmortem.
Jordan Park: taking over. I'll keep the channel updated and coordinate post-incident RCA with Pete and Leah.
incident-bot: On-call handover: Amy Chen -> Jordan Park at 06:30 UTC. Handoff notes saved.
Leah Gomez: sending customer note now. ACME acknowledged and will report if they see new issues. :thumbsup:
Jordan Park: logging final watchstart=06:30 watchend=07:00. If no recurrence by 07:00 UTC, we'll transition to postmortem and mitigation write-up.
Amy Chen: closing loop for now. Great job team. :tada:
